event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: DOC’s 2021 filing portrays COVID-19 as the single most material, near-term threat to its operating model.  The disclosures blend backward-looking data (e.g., 2020 occupancy collapsing by 8-10 percentage points and immediate project shutdowns) with forward-looking warnings (cash-flow erosion, continued rent deferrals, labour shortages, re-suspension of construction).  Language is unequivocal—“material cost increases”, “significant decrease in cash receipts”, “adversely affected”—and repeatedly ties those impacts directly to pandemic-related health measures.  Quantified evidence (occupancy drop from 83.2 % to 75.3 %) and explicit references to development halts demonstrate real, already-incurred harm, not merely hypothetical risk.  Because the filing date (Feb-2021) is well within three years of the event’s onset (Mar-2020), the Time Decay Principle allows high severity scores.  No meaningful mitigating offsets (such as insurance coverage or permanent rent-escalators) are offered; most statements emphasise uncertainty and continued deterioration.  Accordingly, individual sentences score in the upper range (7-9), collectively signalling a high, persistent pandemic risk profile for DOC.

evidence_list.snippet: The COVID-19 pandemic and health and safety measures intended to reduce its spread have adversely affected, and may continue to adversely affect, our business, results of operations and financial condition.

components.reason: Explicitly links pandemic to adverse impact already realised ('have adversely affected').
States ongoing exposure ('may continue to adversely affect').
Touches three fundamental areas – business, operations, financial condition – indicating breadth of risk.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Direct admission of present and continuing harm across all key performance dimensions warrants a high severity score.

evidence_list.snippet: Within our SHOP and CCRC properties, average occupancy declined from 83.2% and 85.6%, respectively, for the year ended December 31, 2019, to 75.3% and 81.4%, respectively, for the year ended December 31, 2020 and we expect occupancy rates will continue to decline for at least the duration of the COVID-19 pandemic due to a reduction in, or in some cases prohibitions on, new tenant move-ins due to “shelter-in-place” and local health department orders, stricter move-in criteria, lower inquiry volumes, and reduced in-person tours, as well as incidences of COVID-19 outbreaks at our facilities or the perception that outbreaks may occur.

components.reason: Provides concrete, quantified decline in occupancy (about 8-10 percentage points).
Lists multiple causal mechanisms directly tied to pandemic measures (shelter-in-place, stricter criteria, etc.).
Projects further deterioration (‘will continue to decline’).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Detailed, quantified damage plus forecast of ongoing losses pushes this to near-maximum severity.

evidence_list.snippet: Our senior housing property operators are also facing material cost increases as a result of higher staffing hours and compensation, as well as increased usage and inventory of critical medical supplies and personal protective equipment.

components.reason: Identifies immediate cost inflation in critical inputs (staff, PPE).
Uses strong qualifier 'material', signalling magnitude.
Details multiple cost drivers, indicating systemic pressure.
Effect is current (“are facing”), not hypothetical.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Present-tense, multi-factor cost spike with ‘material’ language merits a high score.

evidence_list.snippet: We temporarily suspended development and redevelopment projects in the greater San Francisco and Boston areas as a result of the “shelter-in-place” orders and local, state and federal directives.

components.reason: Describes direct operational shutdown (suspension of projects).
Specifies geographic concentration (San Francisco & Boston), heightening exposure.
Causally linked to pandemic-driven government orders.
Indicates action already taken, confirming realised impact.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Concrete suspension of capital projects illustrates tangible disruption, justifying a strong risk score.

evidence_list.snippet: Within our medical office portfolio, many physician practices temporarily discontinued outpatient procedures and nonessential surgeries in 2020 due to health and safety measures, which negatively impacted their cash flows.

components.reason: Notes tenants halting core revenue-generating activities.
Connects stoppage directly to pandemic health measures.
Highlights negative cash-flow consequence for tenants, implying rent-payment risk.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Tenant revenue shock endangers rent collections; explicit link to pandemic drives elevated severity.

evidence_list.snippet: Rent deferrals or delays in rent commencement for tenants may result in a significant decrease in our cash receipts during the period of the deferrals;

components.reason: Forecasts direct hit to liquidity ('significant decrease in our cash receipts').
Specifies mechanism—rent deferrals/delays—tied to pandemic concessions.
Forward-looking conditional risk adds uncertainty.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Potential for ‘significant’ cash shortfall from rent deferrals signals high financial exposure.

evidence_list.snippet: The impact on our results of operations and financial condition resulting from (i) suspensions or delays in development and redevelopment activities and tenant improvement projects, including due to local, state and federal orders or guidelines, delays or increased costs caused by slow-downs in construction as a result of implementing social distancing and other health and safety protocols, or delays or increased costs caused by a shortage of construction materials or labor, as well as potential postponement of rent commencement dates due to delays in tenant improvement projects, and (ii) a decrease in acquisitions and dispositions of properties compared to historical levels;

components.reason: Enumerates multiple pandemic-driven operational and financial disruptions.
Links directly to results of operations and financial condition.
Highlights supply-chain and labour shortages, broadening risk scope.
Covers both current suspensions and future transactional slowdowns.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Comprehensive list of operational bottlenecks underscores multi-dimensional risk at substantial severity.

evidence_list.snippet: For example, increased operating expenses at our SHOP and CCRC properties, including due to labor shortages, as well as increased screening and protective measures intended to prevent an outbreak and/or slow the spread of a COVID-19 outbreak, has adversely affected and is expected to continue to adversely affect the cash flow from operations we receive from the affected properties.

components.reason: Affirms cash-flow deterioration already occurring and expected to persist.
Cites concrete drivers—labour shortages, screening, protective measures.
Uses strong adverse wording twice (‘adversely affected’).
Example illustrates depth of impact on key asset classes (SHOP & CCRC).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Current and continuing cash-flow hit across flagship segments elevates the snippet’s risk score.
